title: Chapter 50
content:
"Didn't sleep well?"

Yu-jung asked, studying Il-hyun’s face with genuine concern.

"No. I've just been forcing smiles for people I can't stand since dawn. It's making me nauseous."

His sharp, cutting tone made Yu-jung force an awkward smile, her eyes darting around the banquet floor. Today was supposed to be a grand celebration—his formal inauguration as Executive Director—yet his lethal, brooding expression made him look like a man dressed for a bloodbath. Besieged by a relentless stream of guests offering congratulations, Il-hyun finally asked Yu-jung for painkillers. She fished a blister pack from her handbag and pressed it into his palm.

Ducking away from the crowd, Il-hyun swallowed the tablets, slipped into the executive restroom, and splashed freezing water over his face. Massaging his temples to dull the throbbing ache behind his eyes, he checked his watch.

Roughly forty minutes remained until the strike window.

He blotted his face with a linen towel, staring into his own reflection. Perhaps from the lack of sleep—or something far more insidious—his dark irises were honed to a razor's edge.

Pausing, he checked the snug fit of the concealed ballistic vest beneath his dress shirt, reached into his jacket, and pulled out his burner phone. He dialed a single, secure speed-dial.

"It's me."

[Yes, Director. Go ahead.]

"Are you in position?"

[Stationed directly on the floor below the sniper's nest.]

Il-hyun fell silent for a heartbeat. Over the line, Park Tae-soo waited patiently for the order.

"Keep him breathing," Il-hyun said quietly. "If he's going to die, I'll put him in the ground with my own hands."

[Understood, sir.]

Ending the call, Il-hyun let out a hollow, self-deprecating laugh. I've completely lost my mind. It would be infinitely cleaner to wipe the kid out on the spot. What was so captivating about that little stray that he needed to see that face one last time before pulling the trigger? Brainless bastard.

Tossing the crumpled towel into the bin with a dark, wry smirk, he stepped back out into the hall.

Down the carpeted corridor, Chairman Kang entered the venue flanked by his mistress, Kim Sun-young, and a subdued Kang Seok-joo.

Il-hyun smoothed his expression instantly, stepping forward with an effortless, filial smile. "You've arrived, Father."

"Indeed. You seem to have prepared thoroughly."

"Assemblyman Yoon and Minister Park have been waiting in the VIP lounge for quite some time."

Chairman Kang nodded with a benign, grandfatherly smile, leading Kim Sun-young inside. Seok-joo cast a wary, nervous glance toward Il-hyun before scurrying after them.

Watching the patriarch's receding back, the warmth in Il-hyun’s eyes froze into pure, unadulterated ice.

Enjoy the spotlight while you still have breath in your lungs, Father.

Across the street, Jakyeong rolled his neck from side to side, working the stiffness from his shoulders. After stretching his limbs, he walked up to the tinted floor-to-ceiling glass. The heavy solar film completely masked the interior from the outside world.

He settled the heavy precision rifle onto the bipod, inching the match-grade barrel forward through a slit in the window casing.

Ryun’s voice crackled through the encrypted earpiece.

[All green on your end?]

"Yeah. What about your position?"

[Holding in the extraction zone. You see the blue utility van?]

Jakyeong shifted his gaze down to street level. Parked along the curb outside a boutique café was a blue work van, flanked closely by Ryun’s unmarked sedan.

"Visual confirmed."

Twenty minutes to the shot.

Popping a piece of mint gum into his mouth, Jakyeong chewed slowly, forcing his heart rate down to a steady, rhythmic baseline. He leaned his back against the bare concrete beneath the sill, letting the seconds tick away.

Closing his eyes, Kang Il-hyun’s smug, arrogant face drifted into his mind uninvited. Jakyeong gave his head a sharp, violent shake, violently scrubbing the image clean.

He forced his mind toward other fantasies instead: the private tropical island he would buy with eighteen billion won, the gorgeous partner he might settle down with, the sweet kids they'd raise together, and... Kang Il-hyun?

Why the hell is your face popping up there?!

Jakyeong scowled, batting at the empty air in furious frustration. Get lost. Get the fuck out of my head. Yet that infuriating, wicked smirk refused to fade.

"Damn it all."

Cursing under his breath, Jakyeong pushed himself up. Strike window open.

He pressed his eye to the optic, leveling the high-magnification reticle against the panoramic windows of the inauguration hall opposite. Figures glided past the glass.

Then, Kang Il-hyun walked into the crosshairs.

It was time for the inaugural address. Jakyeong slowed his respiration, matching his breaths to an internal metronome. Scanning the perimeter of the podium, familiar faces filled the frame: Kang Yu-jung, Chairman Kang, Seok-joo, and an array of high-ranking syndicate board members.

Following the Chairman's opening remarks, Kang Il-hyun stepped up to the dais. Standing before the bank of microphones, he began his address. He hadn't dressed any differently than usual, yet under the brilliant banquet lights, he looked undeniably striking.

Concluding his speech, Il-hyun stepped out from behind the podium.

The crosshairs drifted down from his face, tracking along his chest. Jakyeong held his breath.

Il-hyun bent at the waist, offering a deep, impeccably polite bow to the applause of the crowd. The reticle smoothly dropped past his sternum, past his stomach, settling directly over his upper thighs.

The split second Il-hyun straightened up, Jakyeong squeezed the match trigger.

Crack!

The high-caliber round shattered the banquet glass, tearing clean through Il-hyun's left thigh.

Il-hyun violently staggered backward. The hall descended into immediate pandemonium—guests vaulting from their seats, security details swarming the stage, and automated steel security shutters rapidly descending over the shattered glass.

Without missing a single beat, Jakyeong racked the heavy bolt, ejecting the smoking brass casing, and sent a second round screaming through the narrowing gap.

Crack!

The second bullet struck home with surgical precision, blowing through his right thigh.

A fountain of dark crimson erupted across the stage floor as Il-hyun collapsed like a marionette with severed strings. The heavy blast shutters slammed shut with a deafening thud, completely cutting off the visual.

Jakyeong broke from the scope, releasing a ragged, burning breath.

BAM! BAM!

The heavy fire door to the office suite buckled violently on its hinges. Shouts of armed men bled through the steel panel.

THUD! CRACK!

A heavy breaching ram was tearing into the locking mechanism.

Without a second's hesitation, Jakyeong pulled two tactical smoke canisters from his belt, primed the pins, and rolled them toward the entrance. Dense, blinding gray chemical smoke billowed across the floorboards.

The moment he clicked his harness carabiner into the pre-rigged descent cable—CRASH!—the door was ripped off its frame.

Heavy tactical boots charged through the smoke. Jakyeong sprinted across the bare concrete, launching his entire body straight through the window.

SHATTER!

Safety glass exploded into glittering hail as he plummeted into the open air. Swinging through the arc of the high-tensile extraction cable, the momentum swung him violently back toward the floor below.

Jakyeong braced his boots, kicking clean through the sixteenth-floor glass and rolling across the carpeted office floor to absorb the kinetic shock.

Terrified office workers shrieked, ducking under cubicles.

Slicing the descent line with a flick of his combat knife, Jakyeong bolted out the suite doors toward the primary fire escape. Taking the concrete stairwell three steps at a time, furious shouts and the rapid drumming of combat boots echoed from the landings above.

BANG! BANG!

Rounds ricocheted off the steel handrails, sending deafening metallic shrieks ripping through the narrow shaft.

Rounding the fourteenth-floor landing, a squad of heavily armed enforcers came charging up from below.

Jakyeong vaulted over the handrail, driving both combat boots straight into the lead man's chest. Landing over the tumbling body, his blade flashed in a blur of rapid-fire strikes, severing hamstrings and quadriceps in brutal, disabling sweeps.

A guard raised a sidearm from the lower landing; Jakyeong hauled a bleeding body up as a human shield, simultaneously launching his combat knife in a fluid, overhand throw. The steel blade buried to the hilt in the shooter's throat.

Too many of them. Breaking through this bottleneck alive on foot was impossible.

Jakyeong kicked open the nearest fire door, bursting onto the active office floor. Seeing a figure drenched in arterial blood, workers erupted into hysterical screams.

Jakyeong seized a heavy rolling chair, hurled it through the exterior window, and leaped onto the shattered sill. The enforcers breached the office doors behind him, weapons raised. The floor descended into absolute hell.

Jakyeong threw himself out into empty air.

He struck the roof of a parked SUV below with a bone-jarring crash, collapsing the roof pillars and shattering the windshield.

A hail of automatic fire immediately rained down from the upper windows, asphalt chipping and sparking around him. Jakyeong rolled off the crumpled hood, crawling beneath the undercarriage as rounds chewed through the pavement inches from his boots.

His earpiece buzzed with Ryun’s frantic voice.

[Status! Where are you?!]

"Rear service parking! Move your ass!"

A split second later, the roar of a modified V8 engine tore through the alley. Ryun’s black sedan drifted into the lot with screaming tires. The passenger door flew open, and Jakyeong scrambled out from beneath the chassis, diving inside headfirst.

Rounds hammered the sedan from above, spiderwebbing the glass into opaque white fractures.

Ryun floored the accelerator, tearing out of the commercial lot into the main thoroughfare.

Panting in ragged heaves, Jakyeong collapsed against the leather seat. A sharp, burning ache flared in his left arm—looking down, his sleeve was soaked in dark, spreading crimson.

Ryun threw a frantic glance across the console. "You hit?!"

"Grazed. I'm fine."

Checking the rearview mirror, Ryun let out a vicious curse.

Multiple black SUVs had aggressively peeled out of the intersecting avenues, pursuing them at breakneck speeds. The midday lull between rush hours was a double-edged sword: the clear lanes allowed them to weave at terminal velocity, but their pursuers weren't dropping an inch.

"Those bastards are out for blood!" Ryun shouted, a wild, adrenaline-fueled grin splitting his face.

Jakyeong reached into the rear footwell, hauling up a compact tactical assault rifle.

Ahead, the yawning concrete mouth of a highway tunnel loomed.

Slapping a fresh magazine into the magwell, Jakyeong’s face settled into a mask of pure, clinical detachment.

Ryun tapped the brakes hard as they crossed into the tunnel. Sensing an opening, the lead pursuit SUVs surged forward, bumper-to-bumper.

BANG! BANG!

Rounds punched through their rear windshield, chewing into the upholstery. Ducking low over the wheel, Ryun cursed himself for skipping the bulletproof glass package.

Jakyeong kicked out the shattered remnants of the front windshield with two heavy strikes of his boot, locking eyes with Ryun beneath the tunnel lights.

"Do it."

Ryun yanked the steering wheel hard into a violent J-turn.

Tires shrieked in agony as the sedan executed a complete 180-degree spin, hurtling backward down the tunnel in high-speed reverse.

Through the gaping hole where the windshield used to be, Jakyeong brought the rifle to his shoulder and unleashed sustained, fully automatic fire.

RAT-TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT!

A relentless wall of lead hammered the pursuing convoy, shredding radiators, punching through driver-side windshields, and blowing out front tires.

The lead SUV lost steering, fish-tailing violently before flipping onto its roof in a shower of sparks. The secondary vehicles collided into the tumbling wreckage with concussive, crunching impacts, spinning into the tunnel walls in plumes of thick black smoke.

Ryun wrenched the wheel back, whipping the car forward with a roaring spin, letting out a booming, triumphant laugh.

"That's my fucking boy! Pure Lee Ja-kyeong!"

Ryun held out a celebratory fist, but Jakyeong tossed the empty rifle into the rear seat, his energy completely spent as he let his head fall back against the headrest.

Hot, humid summer air rushed through the shattered frame, carrying the heavy, nauseating stench of spent gunpowder and blood. It was an odor he had lived with his entire life, yet today, it made his stomach churn with profound revulsion.

He lit a fresh cigarette, letting his eyelids fall shut.

I'm sick of it. Sick of this whole fucking world.

The vivid image of Kang Il-hyun collapsing in a fountain of blood flashed before his eyes, pulling a bitter, hollow smirk to his lips.

You brought this on yourself.

After all... you were planning to put me in the ground the moment the trigger was pulled anyway.
